simple.meaning: חֹק (chôq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “an enactment ; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 128 times across Genesis, Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, and 11 more, beginning at Genesis 47:22. Its contexts include family line, commandment, kingship, priesthood, land, Egypt.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֹק (H2706).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: חֹק (chôq) / H2706 is traced through Genesis 47:22, Genesis 47:26, Exodus 5:14, Exodus 12:24 as a generated source-based concept entry.
